required_audit_coverage.detail: report has 23 Required Audit answer/question alignment issue(s)
required_audit_items: Was this packet promoted to `project_state/decision_packet.md` before execution?
Was execution started from a fresh branch based on current `main` rather than PR #5 or PR #6?
Was v10 recorded as `REWORK_REQUIRED` and strategically superseded rather than accepted?
Did PR #5 remain unchanged and frozen at the audited head?
Was PR #5 compared against the activation-time `main`?
Does the capability inventory cover every material changed file in PR #5?
Are capabilities grouped by function rather than by historical round alone?
Does every capability identify implementation files, tests, artifacts, dependencies, and current-main overlap?
Does every capability have exactly one primary disposition category?
Are useful v10 Workflow changes classified independently from legacy report/closeout machinery?
Are existing command-plan, execution-log, report-summary, closeout, policy-lint, prompt-consistency, jobs, Runner, User Solve, CI, context, manifest, and evidence capabilities explicitly inventoried?
Does the authority matrix assign BMAD only to SDLC/planning responsibilities?
Does it assign one primary runtime candidate and prohibit dual-primary runtime architecture?
Does it assign GitHub as the source of truth for branch, commit, PR, review, CI, merge, and release facts?
Does it reserve high-risk authorization and binary-analysis trust semantics for reverse-agent?
Does the migration disposition identify capabilities that are self-maintenance of the legacy control plane?
Does the selective migration manifest provide file-level keep/adapt/archive/drop instructions?
Does the baseline recommendation explicitly choose `CURRENT_MAIN`, `PR5`, or `SELECTIVE_INTEGRATION_BASELINE` and justify the choice?
Does the baseline recommendation include rollback and compatibility implications?
Does the transition packet define the first follow-on implementation Decision with exact scope and non-goals?
Are roadmap/workstream entries updated without becoming execution authority?
Were no frameworks installed and no product/runtime code changed?
Were targeted tests actually run and recorded in `pytest_result.txt`?
Does the final report list actual changed files based on Git diff rather than a hand-written incomplete list?
Are all Required Audit answers question-specific rather than template repetition?
Did local final-check and closeout run, or was any legacy-only failure explicitly recorded without spawning another repair round?
Was no remote State Gate success claimed or required?
Is the next action a concrete implementation Decision rather than “continue improving”?
